# OSSL to Fukushima transfer


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

<div>

> **Work in progress**

</div>

This project tests whether CNN models of soil mid-infrared (MIR)
spectra, trained on the [Open Soil Spectral Library
(OSSL)](https://explorer.soilspectroscopy.org/), help predict soil
properties from spectra of Fukushima soils. OSSL was measured on Bruker
instruments and the Fukushima soils on a Thermo Nicolet. The targets are
exchangeable potassium (Kex), cation exchange capacity (CEC) and the
ratio of exchangeable to total Cs-137. The Fukushima data are 1,389 soil
samples from 391 fields, sampled from 2013 to 2020.

The audience is soil scientists working with the Fukushima data and
anyone transferring spectral models between instruments. Each notebook
asks one question. The table under “Notebooks” gives each question and
its answer. The questions under “Questions for the Fukushima data team”
need answers from the people who sampled and measured the soils.

## Findings

OSSL models fail on the Fukushima spectra without retraining. Without
fine-tuning, the OSSL Kex model gives R² below 0 and a correlation of
0.13 on the Fukushima test samples. The OSSL CEC model gives a
correlation of 0.57, with a large bias.

Trained on Fukushima labels, OSSL helps Kex a little on fields already
seen in training, and not at all on new fields. On the Cs137 study’s
test samples, full fine-tuning gives Kex R² 0.41 against 0.37 for a CNN
trained on Fukushima only. For CEC it gives 0.74 against 0.71. When
whole fields are held out, ridge regression on frozen OSSL features
gives Kex R² 0.26 against 0.28 for ridge regression on the spectra.

For the Cs-137 ratio, frozen OSSL features help on new fields, but only
slightly. All three models below use ridge regression, scored with folds
grouped by field; only the input changes. Ridge on the preprocessed
spectra (SNV, then a Savitzky-Golay first derivative) gives R² 0.52.
Ridge on the activations of block 4 of the two CNNs trained on OSSL to
predict Kex and CEC, with their weights frozen, gives R² 0.57. Ridge on
block 4 of the same CNNs with random weights gives R² 0.52, the same as
the spectra. The gain of 0.05 (bootstrap interval over fields 0.017 to
0.077) therefore comes from what the networks learned on OSSL, not from
the network architecture. It cuts the unexplained variance from 48% to
43%.

Scores on the Cs137 study’s split are optimistic. 89% of its 398 test
samples come from a field that also has samples in training. Holding out
whole fields lowers Kex R² by 0.10 to 0.13 and the Cs-137 ratio by 0.05
to 0.08.

The OSSL soils cover the Fukushima soils in property space. The OSSL Kex
model predicts the closest OSSL soil to each Fukushima soil at R² 0.60.
Removing the Bruker-Thermo difference from the spectra, and augmenting
the spectra during pretraining, both left its Kex correlation on the
Fukushima spectra near 0. Water vapour and sample moisture do not
explain the failure.

In Fukushima’s Lowland soils, the sharp clay-mineral bands near 3620 and
3695 cm⁻¹ relate to clay in the opposite direction to OSSL. Band depth
is measured in each spectrum as minus the minimum of its second
derivative near the band centre. In the Lowland soils, deeper bands go
with less clay (Spearman -0.31 and -0.35, 631 samples). In the OSSL
soils with the closest lab properties, deeper bands go with more clay
(0.28 and 0.39). The OSSL Kex model relies most on this region, so this
is one sign that OSSL’s spectral relations do not hold in Fukushima
soils. It has not been shown to cause the Kex failure.

On new fields, Kex can hardly be predicted within paddy fields. Ridge
regression on the spectra gives R² -0.03 in paddy fields and 0.20 in
upland fields. Paddy fields hold 880 of the 1,388 samples with Kex.

## Questions for the Fukushima data team

1.  Fields: does each `field_no` name the same field in every year?
    `20_grouped_cv` assumes it does.
2.  Potassium fertilisation: which fields received extra K after 2011 to
    limit Cs-137 uptake, and from when? Added K leaves no mineral
    signature in the spectra. If the paddy fields received it, that
    would explain why the spectra cannot rank Kex within paddy fields.
3.  Kex method: is `soil_ex_K2O` in mg K₂O per 100 g of dry soil, and
    which extraction gave it? OSSL uses 1 M ammonium acetate at pH 7.
    The project assumes mg K₂O per 100 g and divides by 47.1 to get
    cmolc/kg.
4.  Other units: are `soil_MgO` and `soil_CaO` in mg of oxide per 100 g
    of dry soil, and `soil_C` and `soil_N` in %? The comparisons with
    OSSL in `12_wetchem` depend on these conversions.
5.  Clay: which method measured `clay`, and does it differ between soil
    types or years? If the clay values in the Lowland soils are suspect,
    the comparisons in `12_wetchem`, `18_aloh` and `19_cs137_inside`
    need revisiting.
6.  Clay mineralogy: which clay minerals dominate the Lowland paddy
    soils? Do mineralogy data, such as XRD or oxalate-extractable Al and
    Si, exist for any samples? If the mineralogy is unusual, models
    trained on Fukushima labels are the way forward rather than OSSL.
7.  Sample preparation: how were the samples dried, ground and, if at
    all, diluted for each instrument? Did the Bruker and Thermo scans of
    the paired soils use the same prepared material? The answers decide
    which spectral corrections are realistic.
8.  Instruments: which accessory, resolution and purging did the Thermo
    Nicolet use? Which Bruker instrument and accessory measured the
    paired soils?
9.  Doubtful scans: `00_data` leaves out 12 samples whose scans disagree
    between operators or between file exports. Which scans are right?
    The answer can bring these samples back.

## Set-up

The project uses the soilspec packages
([soilspecdl](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspecdl),
[soilspecdata](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspecdata) and
[soilspectfm](https://github.com/franckalbinet/soilspectfm)) as editable
installs from sibling folders:

    soilspec/
      ossl-fuku-transfer/
      soilspecdl/
      soilspecdata/
      soilspectfm/

Clone the four repositories into one folder, then, in
`ossl-fuku-transfer/`:

``` sh
uv sync --extra dev
```

The Fukushima data is not public. This repository does not contain it.
With access to it, put it in `data/fukushima/` in the workspace folder,
beside the project folders, or set `SOILSPEC_DATA` to the folder that
holds `fukushima/`. `nbdev-test` skips the cells that read the data. Run
`nbdev-test --flags fukudata` to include them.
